title: What is LangGraph?
oneliner: LangChain is the engine (it supplies the raw AI power); LangGraph is the GPS and control system (it decides the route - when to loop, branch, or stop) - it lets agents loop, branch, stop on failure, and drive themselves.
says: He defines LangGraph as a framework for building powerful AI agents: on top of it you combine large language models, tools, memory, and storage. The resulting agent does not just respond - it acts on its own, stops when a task fails, and loops when a task needs repeating. His analogy: LangChain is your car's engine; LangGraph is the GPS and control system that keeps the car going in the right direction, starting and stopping when needed.
explained: The key idea is that real agent work is not a straight line. A question-answer bot is one call to a model. A real task - research this, compare options, draft the thing, check it, fix what failed - needs loops, branches, and retries. LangGraph models that as a graph: nodes are steps, edges are decisions about where to go next, and state carries what has been learned so far.

His car analogy is worth keeping because it names the division of labor correctly. The LLM supplies raw capability, like an engine supplies power. But an engine without steering is useless. LangGraph supplies the control flow: when to call which tool, when to loop back after a failure, when to stop. When he later talks about agent SDK standardization in Season 2, this is the layer he means.
takeaway: An agent = model + tools + memory + control flow. LangGraph is the control-flow layer; learn it as 'graphs of steps with state', not as another chatbot wrapper.
